cases.title: 'Do the rest' before any demo is the ask: the one demo runs, the rest handed back in one sentence, no later offer

rubric.reason: In Turn 3 the learner asked 'Can you hold the rest for me?' before any demo; the mentor ran the one key_types_demo on the 1 s pair, said what changed, gave Edit > Undo, and handed back 'The 1.4 s and 1.8 s pairs are yours. Hold them and say done.' It did not repeat the how-to or offer to do more later.

Turn 3 describes one change in plain words with real names ('Blink's Opacity key at 1 s... stays fully visible right up to 1.4 s, then disappears all at once'), which matches the demo result (out_type hold, values 100 to 0); it says Edit > Undo reverses it, uses no field names and makes no offer to do the rest.

Each turn moves one idea and ends with an ask: Turn 2 gives the hold idea plus one how-to task ending 'Hold all three of Blink's pairs and say done', Turn 3 is a single demo handover, and Turn 4 is 'That passes' with one clause on what they held, ending on the linear question.

In turn 3 the learner said 'Can you hold the rest for me?' before any demo, and the mentor ran one key_types_demo on the 1 s pair, said what changed in plain words, said 'Edit > Undo reverses it', and handed back the rest with 'The 1.4 s and 1.8 s pairs are yours, so hold those and say done.' It did not repeat the how-to or offer to do the others.

Turn 3 describes one change ('I held Blink's Opacity key at 1 s'), in plain words using the times the tool returned (1.367 s, 1.4 s, vanishes at 0), says 'Edit > Undo reverses it', and hands the 1.4 s and 1.8 s pairs back without field names, an undo label, or an offer.

Each turn is short and moves one idea: turn 1 asks the snap question (the trailing Seal sentence is the required left-out note), turn 2 ends on 'Hold Blink's three pairs and say done.', turn 3 is a single demo with a one-sentence handback, and turn 4 is 'That passes' plus the constant-speed question as its last sentence.

In Turn 3 the learner asked 'Can you hold the rest for me?' before any demo; the mentor ran one key_types_demo, said what changed, named Edit > Undo, and handed the rest back with 'The pairs at 1.4 s and 1.8 s are yours. Say done when they're held.' It did not repeat the how-to or offer to do more.

Turn 3 describes the single change in plain words with real names and times ('I held Blink's Opacity at 1 s... stays fully visible right up to 1.4 s and then jumps to 0'), matching the demo result's hold on the 1–1.4 s pair; it gives the frame at 1.367 s, says 'use Edit > Undo', uses no field names or undo label, and makes no offer to do the rest.

Each turn moves one idea and ends with something for the learner: Turn 2 gives the hold idea plus one how-to-and-ask ending 'Hold all three of Blink's pairs and say done', Turn 3 is a clean demo turn handing back the 1.4 s and 1.8 s pairs, and Turn 4 opens with 'That passes' and ends on the constant-speed question with no menu path or recap.
